description:
## Problem
Trade.txt, TradeHistory.txt, CashTransaction.txt, HoldingHistory.txt, WatchHistory.txt and DailyMarket.txt complete Batch 1. The reviews found the old generator drew trade, account, customer and company keys independently (35 of 1,300 trades had an account belonging to the trade's customer) and did not derive holdings or cash from trades.

## Owner decisions (choice dialogs, 2026-11-20)
- Generator: "BenchBox's own." Strict clean room.
- Word lists: "Small BenchBox-authored word lists committed to the repository (synthetic names, streets, cities; real US state and postal formats where the specification's rules need them). No new dependency, fully deterministic."
- Scale: "Smallest publishable 3; default 5; standard list 3, 5, 10, 100. Values below 3 are allowed for tests and local trials, never publishable." Unit: 5,000 customers per scale factor.
- Data-quality errors: "Inject them. Use the rate the specification or paper states where one exists; where neither states one, use 1 row in 1,000 for that error type, recorded in the generator's report."

## Change
Add writers for the six files. Trades reference existing accounts and securities; trade history is consistent with trade status; holdings and cash transactions derive from completed trades; daily market covers every security for every trading day so 52-week highs and lows can be computed. Inject the trade data-quality errors (invalid commission, invalid charge) at the decided rates and record the counts.

## Clean-room rule (owner: "Strict clean room: the implementer reads only the specification, the paper and the TPC appendix SQL.")
The implementer reads only the TPC-DI v1.1.0 specification, the VLDB 2014 paper (Poess, Rabl, Jacobsen, Caufield) and the TPC appendix SQL. It never opens PDGF configuration or dictionaries, DIGen or PDGF source or decompiled classes, the `tpc-di_src.jar` plugin source, or `shannon-barrow/databricks-tpc-di`'s `tpcdi_gen`. Subagents get the same rule in their brief. The pull request description states that the rule was followed.

## Decision gates
The specification requires DIGen, so this generator's data is non-compliant by definition; the result label covers it. Every distribution, ratio or constant the specification and paper do not state is listed in the pull request description with the value chosen and why, and shown to the owner before arming. Generation runs under the run deadline (`RunDeadline`), with no fixed timeout; this needs run-timeout step 1b merged. If a file format cannot be determined from the specification text alone, stop and ask; do not consult DIGen output.

## Verification rubric
Pass: format fixtures from the specification for each file; consistency tests: every trade's account exists, every holding and cash row traces to a trade, statuses follow the allowed transitions, daily market has no gaps; trade type and status values are exactly the specification's; injected counts equal a recount; byte-identical across runs; generation at scale 3 through `make heavy-run` with time, bytes and peak memory recorded; `make pr-preflight` passes.

## Guardrails (owner, 2026-11-20)
- The agent never posts a stand-in review, closes and reopens a pull request to restart CI, uses `--no-verify`, force-pushes, rewrites an author, or deletes anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`.
- Arming: `make pr-arm` once; one more attempt only when the refusal named a cause, the agent reported it and the cause is cleared; never a third without asking. `make pr-rerun` at most once and only for a job the runner never ran or cancelled, never for a failed test.
- Review threads: reply; resolve only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise the finding again.
- Subagents are read-only. No file edit by script; use the edit tool. Do not edit a pull request description while its CI is starting; post a comment.
- Any limit, default, threshold, status token, message or label text the owner has not already chosen (see tpcdi-correction-plan-20261120) is shown to the owner before it is committed.
- A blocked step stops this item; no workaround. No live cloud run. Heavy work only through `make heavy-run`. One pull request for this item, merged before the next item starts.
- From the quarantine step until the reopening step, no TPC-DI entry point may produce a result that reads PASSED or is admitted for publication.
